import { Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'

<Meta title="Design system/Introduction" />

# Coach Poulpy design system

The app is calm and rounded, like the plush: one blue accent for actions, white or near-white surfaces, and only Poulpy and the Home header tint with his mood. Values live in [`design/tokens.json`](https://github.com/tkint/coach-poulpy/blob/main/design/tokens.json) and are generated into each platform (see [`design/README.md`](https://github.com/tkint/coach-poulpy/blob/main/design/README.md)); these rules say how to use them. The live swatches are on the [Tokens](?path=/docs/design-system-tokens--docs) page of the component workshop.

The landing site, the web app and these pages draw with one package, [`web/ui`](https://github.com/tkint/coach-poulpy/tree/main/web/ui): DaisyUI with the Poulpy theme and a few Vue components on top ([ADR 0023](https://tkint.github.io/coach-poulpy/docs/adr/0023-the-websites-share-one-vue-and-daisyui-design-system)). This workshop is its home ([ADR 0028](https://tkint.github.io/coach-poulpy/docs/adr/0028-storybook-is-the-component-workshop-of-the-design-system), [ADR 0029](https://tkint.github.io/coach-poulpy/docs/adr/0029-mockups-are-stories-in-the-component-workshop)).

- **Rules**: how to use [colour](?path=/docs/design-system-rules-colour--docs), [type](?path=/docs/design-system-rules-type--docs), [space, radius and motion](?path=/docs/design-system-rules-space-radius-and-motion--docs), [icons](?path=/docs/design-system-rules-icons--docs), [accessibility](?path=/docs/design-system-rules-accessibility--docs), the [components](?path=/docs/design-system-rules-components--docs), the [screens](?path=/docs/design-system-rules-screens--docs) and the [websites](?path=/docs/design-system-rules-websites--docs).
- [Tokens](?path=/docs/design-system-tokens--docs): every value, read from `design/tokens.json`.
- **Core**: what is the same on every platform: Poulpy and the body map. They are drawn here with the web components.
- **Web > Components**: each Vue component in every state, with its classes. Each state is a story and runs as a test in CI, with an accessibility check. Use the toolbar to switch between light and dark.
- **Mobile > Components**: the raw pieces of the Android and iOS screens (buttons, chips, fields, rows), one page each, with a story per variation and controls to try them.
- **Mobile > Patterns**: pieces composed from those, such as the nav bar, sheets and charts.
- **Mobile > Screens**: every agreed phone screen, built from the components and patterns, and the drafts ([ADR 0029](https://tkint.github.io/coach-poulpy/docs/adr/0029-mockups-are-stories-in-the-component-workshop)).

## Classes

Every DaisyUI class carries the `cp-` prefix (`cp-btn`, not `btn`); the few classes of our own (`cp-chip`, `cp-stepper`, `cp-type-*`...) never reuse a DaisyUI name. Tailwind's own utilities (`w-full`, `bg-secondary`) have no prefix. A component's docs page lists the classes it renders.

Type has plain classes and no component: `cp-type-display`, `cp-type-title`, `cp-type-headline`, `cp-type-label`.

design-system-rules-colour--docs.content:
import { Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'

<Meta title="Design system/Rules/Colour" />

# Colour

## Colour roles

Use roles, never raw palette steps, in screens. Each role has a light and a dark value.

| Role | Use it for |
| --- | --- |
| `primary` / `onPrimary` | The main action on a screen (Start session, Save), selected chips, links, progress |
| `primaryContainer` / `onPrimaryContainer` | Tonal buttons, selected rows, Poulpy's speech on the blue side |
| `grumpy` / `onGrumpy` | The one action offered while Poulpy is on the ember side (Catch up, Flip him back) |
| `grumpyContainer` / `onGrumpyContainer` | The Home header and cards while Poulpy is on the ember side |
| `background`, `surface`, `surfaceVariant` | Screen, cards and sheets, inset fields and steppers |
| `onSurfaceVariant`, `outline` | Secondary text and captions; card borders and dividers |
| `success` | A confirmed save or a finished phase, with a check icon |
| `error` / `onError` | Errors only: crimson, always with an icon and words |
| `heat1`, `heat2`, `heat3` | How much a workout works each muscle on the body map, from a little to most. Orange, on the body map only: never for Poulpy's moods |
| `pain` | A worked area that hurts, outlined on the body map. Purple, so it reads apart from the heat and is never mistaken for an error |

Rules:

- `poulpy.blue`, `poulpy.ember` and `poulpy.ink` are Poulpy's fabric and never change between light and dark.
- The plush blue and ember are too light for white text: buttons use `primary` and `grumpy`.
- Ember means "a session slipped", never "something broke". An error is crimson, so a cross Poulpy is never read as a failure.
- Colours that must be told apart also differ in lightness, not hue alone.


## Mood shades

Six shades, from `mood.*`, only on Poulpy himself, the Home header tint and mood-coloured charts:

| Side | Shades, calmest to strongest |
| --- | --- |
| Blue (on track) | `recovering`, `happy`, `proud` |
| Ember (a session slipped) | `annoyed`, `grumpy`, `fuming` |

Which shade shows when is in [Brand](?path=/docs/brand-moods--docs).

import { Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'

<Meta title="Design system/Rules/Type" />

# Type

Baloo 2 for display and titles, Nunito for everything else. Platforms map each role to a system text style so Dynamic Type and font scaling keep working (`.font(.poulpy(.headline))` on iOS, `MaterialTheme.typography` on Android).

| Role | Font | Size / line | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `display` | Baloo 2 800 | 40 / 44 | Poulpy's line on Home, end-of-session headline |
| `title` | Baloo 2 700 | 28 / 32 | Screen titles, workout name on its page |
| `headline` | Baloo 2 700 | 21 / 25 | Section heads, the current exercise in the player |
| `body` | Nunito 500 | 16 / 24 | Everything you read |
| `label` | Nunito 800, tracked 0.08 em, upper case | 12.5 / 16 | Eyebrows, tab labels, "Next up" |
| `timer` | Nunito 800, tabular figures | 64 / 64 | Timers and rep counts, which must not jitter |

**Words never break.** Translations run longer than English (« Bibliothèque », « Échauffement »), so text is laid out for any length:

- Text in a space of fixed width (tab labels, chips, stat tiles, stepper values) stays on one line and shrinks to fit, never below 9 sp / pt; past that it ends in an ellipsis. `FitText` on Android, `.lineLimit(1).minimumScaleFactor(…)` on iOS, whose tab bar already does it.
- Buttons wrap their label between words rather than shrink it.
- Every other text wraps between words only, never inside one, and never hyphenates.

import { Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'

<Meta title="Design system/Rules/Space, radius and motion" />

# Space, radius and motion

## Space, radius, motion

- Spacing steps: 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48 (`xs` to `xxxl`). Pick a step; never a value between them.
- Radius: 8 for chips and small fields, 10 for cards, rows and buttons, 14 for sheets, pill for chips. Small cards stay close to square so their text reads first.
- Controls stay compact: a button is 40 high by default and follows the size scale of the [Button](?path=/docs/mobile-components-button--docs) (xs 24 to xxl 64), an icon button 40; below 44 the touch area stays 44. The side gutter of a screen is 16, and rows are 56 high with a 32 to 40 avatar. In the apps these come from one place, `PoulpySize` (generated from `design/tokens.json`, next to `PoulpySpace` and `PoulpyRadius`); a screen never writes a literal height, gutter or corner radius.
- Motion: the flip (700 ms with overshoot) is the one signature move, used only when Poulpy changes side. Mood shades fade in 300 ms. Everything else is 150 to 250 ms and plain. With reduced motion on, the loader slows to one swing in 12 s.

import { Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'

<Meta title="Design system/Rules/Icons" />

# Icons

Every icon is from [Lucide](https://lucide.dev), on every platform ([ADR 0024](https://tkint.github.io/coach-poulpy/docs/adr/0024-lucide-is-the-icon-set)). Use its name for the action, never a home-made drawing of one Lucide already has. Icons take their colour from the roles above, and an error keeps its icon. Lucide's drawing stays as it is: a 24 box and a 2 wide round stroke, never filled; only the size changes (24 by default, 20 in chips and small buttons, 16 to 18 beside a line of text).

| Where | How |
| --- | --- |
| Vue (web app, `web/ui`, docs site) | `@lucide/vue`: `<ChevronLeft class="size-5" aria-hidden="true" />` |
| Phone mockups | `<MobileIcon name="chevron-left" :size="20" />`, or the `icon` prop of a `Mobile*` component |
| Android | `Icon(Lucide.ChevronLeft, contentDescription = …)` |
| iOS | `LucideIcon(.chevronLeft, size: 20)`, or `Label("action.back", lucide: .chevronLeft)` |

The Android and iOS icons are generated from `design/icons/`: run `node design/build-icons.mjs --add <name>` for an icon not used yet.

One icon per meaning, the same on every platform:

| Meaning | Lucide icon |
| --- | --- |
| Back, previous; next, open a row | `chevron-left`; `chevron-right` |
| Close, clear | `x` |
| More actions | `ellipsis-vertical` |
| Add; duplicate, copy | `plus`; `copy` |
| Edit; delete | `pencil`; `trash` |
| Share; export a file | `share-2`; `download` |
| Plan a day | `calendar-plus` |
| Error | `circle-exclamation-point` |
| Tabs: Home, Library, Live, History, Settings | `house`, `library-big`, `activity`, `rotate-ccw-clock`, `settings` |
| Warm-up, work, cool down | `sun`, `zap`, `moon` |
| Circuit, sets | `repeat`, `list` |
| Treadmill (no Lucide treadmill), foot pod, heart rate band | `gauge`, `footprints`, `heart-pulse` |
| Filters: equipment, focus, position, zones, tags | `dumbbell`, `target`, `armchair`, `person-standing`, `tag` |

The movement-pattern badge stands in for exercise pictures, and Lucide draws few people, so its icons are the nearest Lucide match rather than an exact one: squat `person-standing`, hinge `hand-grab`, lunge `footprints`, push `dumbbell`, pull `biceps-flexed`, carry `luggage`, core `shield`, rotation `rotate-cw`, locomotion `sport-shoe`, mobility `accessibility`, stretch `stretch-horizontal`.

import { Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'

<Meta title="Design system/Rules/Accessibility" />

# Accessibility

- Touch targets at least 44 by 44; a visually smaller control, such as the 40 icon button, extends its touch area to 44.
- Text contrast at least 4.5:1, including small grey labels; 3:1 only for text 24 px and up.
- Every icon-only button has a label; decorative drawings of Poulpy are hidden from screen readers, and a pose that carries meaning has a description.
- Nothing depends on colour alone: mood changes also change Poulpy's face and words, errors carry an icon.

design-system-rules-components--docs.content:
import { Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'

<Meta title="Design system/Rules/Components" />

# Components

| Component | Shape | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Button](?path=/docs/mobile-components-button--docs) | Rounded square (10 radius), never a pill, on the websites' size scale: xs 24, sm 32, md 40 (the default), lg 48, xl 56, xxl 64; below 44 the touch area still reaches 44 | `MobileButton` in the mockups, `PoulpyButton` on both platforms (`PoulpyButtonKind`, `PoulpyButtonSize`). Primary: one per screen. Tonal (`primaryContainer`): secondary actions. Secondary (2 px `outline`): cancel, less important choices. Grumpy: only the catch-up action while Poulpy is ember. A top bar's button is `sm`, a screen's or sheet's main action `xl`, a card's actions `md` |
| [Chip](?path=/docs/mobile-components-filter-chip--docs) | 32 high, pill; on = `primary`, off = 1.5 px `outline` | Filters (muscle, equipment, format), with `aria-pressed` or selected state; `PoulpyChip` on both platforms |
| Choosing one value | A select field that opens a sheet for a longer list, or a native menu for a short one | Pills and chips are for filters and for view switches; a form asks for a value with a select, never a row of pills |
| [Search field](?path=/docs/mobile-components-search-field--docs) | 44 high, pill, 1.5 px `outline`, `primary` while it holds text, a round clear button | `PillSearchField` on both platforms |
| [Stepper](?path=/docs/mobile-components-stepper--docs) | Inset `surfaceVariant` box, label, minus and plus round buttons of 44 | Sets, reps, load, rest |
| Pattern badge | 44 round, `primaryContainer`, one icon per movement pattern in `onPrimaryContainer` | Stands in for exercise pictures until real images exist |
| Filter row | Search field, a row of chips, then the count line with one action at its right | `ListFilters` on both platforms, shared by the exercise and workout lists |
| Poulpy card | 14 radius, `primaryContainer`, Poulpy happy on the blue side, a title, a line and one primary button | `PoulpyCard`: no results, an empty list |
| Item menu | A long press (iOS context menu) or ⋮; actions with icons, a divider, then the destructive one | Destructive items and their confirmation are `error` with an icon, never ember; the confirmation says what goes and what stays |
| Plan sheet | 14 radius sheet, a month from Monday; past days dimmed, today outlined, planned days `primary` | `PlanSheet` on both platforms; tick several days, save once |
| Error banner | `error` tint, icon plus text | Never ember |
| Loader | Poulpy's outline from underneath, drawn frame by frame from the 3D model with loose tentacles, swinging half a turn each way, once every 3.6 s; `clockwise` is the other version, which only turns one way | `PoulpyLoader` on both platforms; replaces spinners |


## Base fields

The fields every form is built from. Reference mockups: `profile-edit`, the three `profile-*-sheet` pages, `body-log-sheet`, `body-log-height-sheet`, under Mobile > Screens > Profile and settings in the workshop. Build every new form from these, and move old screens to them as they are touched.

| Field | Shape | Behaviour |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Text field](?path=/docs/mobile-components-text-field--docs) | 52 high, 10 radius (`radius.md`), 1.5 px `outline`, label above, `primary` outline on focus | Free text: a name. A note under it in `onSurfaceVariant` |
| [Select field](?path=/docs/mobile-components-select-field--docs) | Same box, the chosen value (or a muted "Not set") and a chevron | Tapping opens a sheet; nothing else is shown on the screen. Never a row of pills |
| [Option sheet](?path=/docs/mobile-patterns-option-sheet--docs) | 14 radius sheet, a title, one row per choice | Single choice: a radio and the sheet closes on tap. Several choices: checkboxes and a Done button. A choice that needs text (Custom pronouns) shows its text field inside the sheet |
| [Number field](?path=/docs/mobile-components-number-field--docs) | Text field with a unit at its right (`bpm`, `kg`, `cm`) | Selects all its text on focus, opens the numeric keyboard, checks the range on leaving. Optional round − and + buttons on both sides (the `number-entry` pattern) for small nudges. Imperial height is two number fields, ft and in. Every numeric value in the app uses it, including the builder's sets, reps, rest between sets, rest and weight (`builder-sets-edit-step`, `builder-circuit-edit-step`); the − and + step by the same amount as before, and the typed value keeps the same limits |
| [Step slider](?path=/docs/mobile-components-step-slider--docs) | A bar of dots, `•--•--•--•--•`, the current label above it, the two ends named below | A fixed scale of five or fewer named steps, inside an option sheet |
| Password field (draft, #272) | Text field with a show or hide eye button inside its right end; a hint under it (`8 characters or more.`) | `password-field` in the mockups. Errors under a field are `error` text with an icon and the field outline turns `error`; a message about the whole form is an error card (`error` outline and text on `surfaceVariant`, with an icon) |
| [Line chart](?path=/docs/mobile-patterns-line-chart--docs) | Grid lines behind the line, the unit at the top of the axis, a value at each grid line, the date range under it | No grid colour that implies good or bad; a weight going up is never red |
| [Empty chart card](?path=/docs/mobile-patterns-empty-chart-card--docs) | `PoulpyCard` shape with Poulpy on the blue side, a line and the one action that adds the first entry | Shown instead of the chart when nothing is logged |
| Body map | A front and a back figure, drawn in the build the person chose in the profile, as a muscle chart with transparent skin, side by side, each area a shape that fills with `primary` when picked; left and right are separate areas | Every area is a checkbox with a name ("Left knee"), so a screen reader and the text summary under the figure say the same. Left is the person's left: the right half of the front figure and the left half of the back one. Used to say where it hurts, and to show what an exercise works |
| Body map heat map ([#244](https://github.com/tkint/coach-poulpy/issues/244), built in #326) | The body map read-only for a whole workout: areas it doesn't work are outlines only, worked areas fill with `heat1`, `heat2` or `heat3` by sets per muscle group compared with the most-worked one (below 40 %, from 40 %, from 75 %); a worked area that hurts gets a 3 px `pain` outline on a `background` halo, drawn above its neighbours; a Less / More legend, with Hurts when something hurts | The figure is one image whose label is the text summary ("shoulders and triceps most, then chest, back and biceps, a little core"), and the heat steps differ in lightness, so nothing depends on colour alone. On the workout page; the format and equipment badges sit under the workout name in the sheet |
| Details sheet ([#244](https://github.com/tkint/coach-poulpy/issues/244), built in #326) | 14 radius sheet over the body map with no scrim; a handle, the workout name at its top, its content, then the action bar | Three stops (peek, half, full), the handle drags or taps between them: dragged down it shows only the name and actions under a full-screen map; half up by default (on the workout page it stops where the exercises start, so a half-open sheet never shows part of an exercise; the map takes the room that frees); full screen its content scrolls, and scrolling down past its top drags the sheet back down. The map keeps the size it has at half while the sheet goes higher. The back and menu buttons float above it at every stop |
| Plan summary ([#244](https://github.com/tkint/coach-poulpy/issues/244), built in #326) | `primaryContainer` row: a calendar icon, "3 sessions planned" over "Next on Fri 30 Oct", and a Change days button | Replaces one pill per planned day on the workout page |

<Meta title="Design system/Rules/Screens" />

# Screens

Every screen mockup is a story in the [component workshop](?path=/docs/design-system-introduction--docs) ([ADR 0029](https://tkint.github.io/coach-poulpy/docs/adr/0029-mockups-are-stories-in-the-component-workshop)): the web screens under Web > Screens, composed from the `Cp*` components, and the phone screens under Mobile > Screens, built from the `Mobile*` components and patterns.

- Build from an agreed mockup. If a screen has none, agree one through a PR before building it.
- Each state of a screen is a story, in light and dark from the workshop's theme toolbar. A new screen or redesign is tagged `draft`; a PR that changes the tag to `agreed` is its approval, and nothing is built from a draft.
- CI runs every story as a test, with the accessibility check.

The mockup is the design reference; this page defines the shared rules and components used to build it.

design-system-rules-websites--docs.content:
import { Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'

<Meta title="Design system/Rules/Websites" />

# Websites

The landing site, the web app, the web screens of the workshop and the docs site share one package, `web/ui`: DaisyUI with the Poulpy theme and a few Vue components ([ADR 0023](https://tkint.github.io/coach-poulpy/docs/adr/0023-the-websites-share-one-vue-and-daisyui-design-system)). Each component, in every state, with the classes it renders and its interaction and accessibility checks, is in the [component workshop](https://tkint.github.io/coach-poulpy/storybook/) ([ADR 0028](https://tkint.github.io/coach-poulpy/docs/adr/0028-storybook-is-the-component-workshop-of-the-design-system)).

- Use the shared components (`CpButton`, `CpChip`...) in Vue, and never restyle a DaisyUI class in an app. A missing shape goes in `web/ui`, with its stories and the classes it renders in its docs, in the same PR.
- Every DaisyUI class carries the `cp-` prefix (`cp-btn cp-btn-primary`). Our own classes (`cp-chip`, `cp-stepper`, `cp-type-label`...) never reuse a DaisyUI name, so the two cannot clash.
- The roles above keep their meaning: `cp-btn-primary` is `primary`, `cp-btn-secondary` is the tonal `primaryContainer`, `cp-btn-accent` is `grumpy` and only for the catch-up action. Never use DaisyUI's `warning` classes: ember is not a warning, and a problem is an `error`.
- Phone and tablet mockups keep their own stylesheet (`web/storybook/stories/mobile/screens/screens.css`): they draw the native screens, which DaisyUI's look does not match.
- Icons on the websites and in every screen come from Lucide, as in the [Icons](?path=/docs/design-system-rules-icons--docs) section ([ADR 0024](https://tkint.github.io/coach-poulpy/docs/adr/0024-lucide-is-the-icon-set)).


## Web sizes

Buttons, fields and icons on the websites share one size scale, set with the `size` prop of the `Cp*` components: `xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`, `xl`, `xxl`. A component without a `size` is `md`. The numbers come from `webSize` in `design/tokens.json` (`--cp-control-*` and `--cp-icon-*` in the generated `tokens.css`); never write a literal height or icon size.

| Size | Button and field height | Icon (`CpIcon`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `xs` | 24 | 12 |
| `sm` | 32 | 16 |
| `md` | 40 (the default) | 20 |
| `lg` | 48 | 24 |
| `xl` | 56 | 32 |
| `xxl` | 64 | 40 |

- Which components take `size`: `CpButton`, `CpTextField`, `CpPasswordField`, `CpSearchField`, `CpSelectField`, `CpMultiSelectField`, `CpChipSelectField`, `CpPagination`, `CpSegmentedControl`, and `CpIcon` for every Lucide icon. Each has a Sizes story in the workshop with a size control.
- A screen's main action is `xl` (56), a card's actions and form fields are `md`, a list's own search is `lg`, and the controls of a filter bar or a table's pagination are `sm`. A control's own icons follow its size.
- Draw an icon with `<CpIcon :icon="Search" size="sm" />`, never a Lucide component with a `size-*` class.
- `CpChip`, `CpAvatar`, `CpBadge`, `CpTextarea` and `CpStepper` keep their own sizes for now.

# Poulpy and the brand

Poulpy is a friendly, reversible plush octopus: blue and smiling by default, with a playful grumpy mood on his ember side. In the app, ember shifts from burnt orange to red as that mood intensifies. **The side is the status** (are you keeping your plan?) **and the shade is the feeling** (what just happened). - [Drawings](?path=/docs/brand-drawings--docs): every portrait, pose and the loader, as generated.

- [Poulpy moves](?path=/docs/brand-poulpy-moves-turning--docs): how he turns, jumps and cheers in 3D, one move a page.

import { Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'

<Meta title="Brand/Character" />

# Character

## Character rules

- **Grumpy is comic, never guilt.** No "you failed", no streak-loss alarms. Even Fuming is a cartoon tantrum.
- **Pain and rehab always win.** Someone who logged pain gets the Patched up pose and the blue side for 72 h, never ember.
- **One way back, always short.** While Poulpy is ember, the catch-up offered is the shortest workout in the plan, and any finished session flips him straight back.
- **Nothing promised, nothing missed.** With no plan, Poulpy stays on the blue side and only reacts to when you last trained.
- **Poulpy never lifts his tentacles.** Every pose keeps the plush's shape and shows the mood with his face, shade, props and small effects. When he jumps, in 3D, they hang under him and follow.
- **At most one notification a day** in Poulpy's voice, and turning them off keeps the mascot.
- **Every line in French and English** from the start.
- **Inclusive by default.** The app is LGBTQ+ friendly, and that is part of the brand: see [Inclusive by default](?path=/docs/brand-inclusive-by-default--docs).


## Tentacles

Poulpy's ring has eight tentacles. Each finished session lights one, and **a lit tentacle never goes dark**: there is no weekly reset, so a quiet month takes nothing away. The eighth makes a **full octopus** (Champion), and the next session starts a new ring. This replaced "eight tentacles a week"; see [Brand decisions](?path=/docs/brand-decisions--docs), decision 11.

import { Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'

<Meta title="Brand/Moods" />

# Moods

| Mood | Side | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Proud | Blue | A personal record, or a full octopus |
| Happy | Blue | A session done, plan on track; the default |
| Recovering | Blue | Rest days, the hours after a hard session, pain or rehab days |
| Annoyed | Ember | Today's planned session isn't done and the evening is coming (the grace period) |
| Grumpy | Ember | A planned session still not done 24 h after its day |
| Fuming | Ember | Two planned sessions missed |


## When each drawing shows

| What happens | Mood | Drawing |
| --- | --- | --- |
| You finish any session | Happy | Flip back to blue with the flip animation; the flip is the reward |
| You set a record | Proud | Cocky, until the end of the day |
| The eighth tentacle lights | Proud | Champion, on the end-of-session screen, on the share card and Home, with its own heading ("Champion!") and quote (“Eight tentacles. No regrets.”) |
| You share a finished session | Happy | Exhausted with a sweatband, under “Well done!” and the quote “Worth it. Probably.”, on the end-of-session screen and on the share card, whether shared straight away or from the history; the card leaves the sets-done line off; never an ember or guilty drawing |
| A hard session ends (effort 8 or more) | Recovering | Exhausted or Side glance, for the rest of the day |
| A planned rest day | Recovering | Sleeping |
| Pain logged, or a rehab session marked too hard | Recovering | Patched up |
| Mid-set, heavy sets | Current | Straining |
| A new goal set | Current | Standing tall |
| Back after a break | Current | Shy |
| Picking a plan, an unknown exercise | Current | Thinking |
| Today's session not done by the evening | Annoyed | Annoyed portrait |
| A session overdue by 24 h | Grumpy | Pouting, with the catch-up offer |
| Two sessions missed | Fuming | Fuming, with the same catch-up offer |
| No plan, 7 days without training | Happy | Sleeping |
| Loading | | The loader, Poulpy from underneath |

Poses marked Current keep whatever mood Poulpy is in. The shared `PoulpyCoach` decides which drawing shows; `PoulpyDrawing` names every drawing.


## The ember side

Only a plan can turn Poulpy ember, through its calendar entries. A planned workout placed by hand is a reminder, not a promise, and never counts. See [Brand decisions](?path=/docs/brand-decisions--docs), decision 12.

- **Annoyed (the grace period).** From 18:00 on an entry's day, while it is still planned, until the end of the next day. The entry can still be done the day after: finishing it then marks it done.
- **Grumpy.** An entry still planned once the day after its day is over: it is missed.
- **Fuming.** Two or more missed entries.
- **Any finished session flips him back.** Entries dated on or before the day of the last finished session never count, whatever their status. Finishing the catch-up, a free session or another entry all work.
- **Only planned entries count.** Done never counts; a moved entry counts on its new date only; a skipped entry never counts, because skipping is an honest choice and the ember side is for sessions left hanging.
- **Rest days never count.** A plan day with no workout has no entry. On a rest day Poulpy sleeps if he is blue and stays ember if he is ember: a rest day doesn't erase a missed session.
- **Pain and rehab win.** For 72 h after pain is logged or a rehab session is marked too hard, Poulpy is blue and Patched up, and entries dated inside those 72 h never count, even afterwards.
- **No enrollment, no ember.** Without an active enrollment the blue-side rules apply.

When several apply, the first wins: pain or rehab, then Fuming, Grumpy, Annoyed, then the blue-side rules.

**The catch-up** is offered with Grumpy and Fuming, and nowhere on the blue side. It is the workout with the shortest estimated duration in the enrolled plan version, the earliest in the plan on a tie. Finishing it flips Poulpy back like any session; it leaves the missed entries as they are, for the person to skip or move. While Annoyed there is no catch-up: today's entry is the way back.

| Mood | Title | Line |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Annoyed | Tick tock / Tic tac | "Today's \{workout\} is still waiting. I'm turning a little orange." / « \{workout\} t’attend encore aujourd’hui. Je commence à virer à l’orange. » |
| Grumpy | Hmph / Pff | "\{workout\} has been waiting since \{day\}. \{minutes\} minutes and I flip back, promise." / « \{workout\} t’attend depuis \{day\}. \{minutes\} minutes et je me retourne, promis. » |
| Fuming | Full lava / Mode lave | "Sessions slipped by and I'm boiling like a kettle. \{minutes\} minutes and I'm blue again." / « Des séances ont filé et je bous comme une bouilloire. \{minutes\} minutes et je redeviens bleu. » |
| Recovering, rest day | Rest day / Jour de repos | "No training today. I'm napping too." / « Pas d’entraînement aujourd’hui. Moi aussi, je fais la sieste. » |

The catch-up button reads "Catch up: \{workout\}, \{minutes\} min" / « Rattrapage : \{workout\}, \{minutes\} min », with a non-breaking space before the colon. In the Grumpy and Fuming lines, `{minutes}` is the catch-up's duration, an ICU plural in the translation files so one minute reads "1 minute". In the Grumpy line, `{workout}` and `{day}` are the oldest missed entry's: `{day}` is its weekday while it is less than a week old ("Thursday" / « jeudi »), its date after that ("12 October" / « le 12 octobre »).

import { Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'

<Meta title="Brand/Inclusive by default" />

# Inclusive by default

Poulpy is a plush with a blue side and a grumpy side, and nobody has to be one or the other. The app and everything around it welcomes LGBTQ+ people, and these rules apply to every screen, string, drawing and notification.

- **Ask only what a feature needs, and make every personal field optional.** Each field says why it is asked and where the answer is used. "Prefer not to say" is always an option and never a dead end: the app works the same without it.
- **Sex and gender are two questions, and the app asks the first only.** Where an estimate (calories, heart rate zones) depends on physiology, the field is called **Sex assigned at birth**, with Female, Male, Intersex and Prefer not to say, and a line saying it is not about gender. Avoid "biological sex", "birth sex" and "gender" for it. The app never asks about gender identity or orientation, and nothing it shows or says is decided by this field.
- **Pronouns are their own optional field**, a select (choosing Custom shows a text field beneath it): She / her, He / him, They / them, Just my name, a custom entry the person types, or Prefer not to say. They only set French agreement and Poulpy's lines. Without an answer, or with Prefer not to say, the wording stays neutral, a custom entry is shown as written but never drives French agreement, and a pronoun is never guessed from a name, a photo or the sex field.
- **Neutral wording first.** Write copy that needs no gender, in French too (« Bienvenue », « C'est fait », not « bienvenu(e) »). When agreement cannot be avoided, use the person's pronouns, and fall back to the neutral form.
- **Poulpy has no gender.** He is a plush; he is "he" only in English by habit and "il" in French because *poulpe* is masculine. Never write a line that depends on who the person is, and never joke about bodies.
- **No body judgement.** Weight, height and age are data. Poulpy never comments on a weight going up or down, charts use the one accent colour and never red or green for "worse" or "better", and the app shows no BMI and sets no weight goal unless the person asks.
- **Drawings and stories show a range of people.** Future share cards, the website and store images show different bodies, ages, genders and families, and may use the rainbow only as a deliberate Pride moment, never as decoration on Poulpy.
- **Review before shipping.** Wording about sex, gender or bodies is read by people from the community before release, and changed when they say so; the owner decides ties.

The reasons and the wording alternatives that were set aside are in [Brand decisions](?path=/docs/brand-decisions--docs#13-inclusive-by-default). The profile fields that follow these rules are on [Profile and settings](https://tkint.github.io/coach-poulpy/docs/profile-and-settings).

<Meta title="Brand/Voice, logo and type" />

# Voice, logo and type

## Voice

Poulpy speaks in short first-person lines, warm and a little cheeky: "6 of 8 tentacles lit. One more and I'm doing a little dance." or "Thursday's run is still waiting. 20 minutes and I flip back, promise." He jokes about himself, never about the person. In French he says *tu*, like a friend, while the rest of the app says *vous*.


## Logo and type

The logo is the same drawing as the in-app Poulpy: a front view of the plush with five visible arms and the ember lining peeking out underneath. The app icon is the 3D Poulpy, happy and blue, on Deep sea in light and dark alike, painted by `design/build-poulpy-pictures.mjs`. In Settings › App › App icon a person can swap it for another face of Poulpy: Proud, Annoyed, Grumpy, Champion or Cocky, each the picture the app already has, fitted into the icon. Choosing an icon is cosmetic; it never changes Poulpy's mood in the app. Headings use Baloo 2, body text Nunito; see the [design system](?path=/docs/design-system-introduction--docs).

import { Meta, Story } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as Live from './Brand.stories'

<Meta title="Brand/Poulpy in 3D" />

# Poulpy in 3D

The plush as a solid you can turn around: a bubble of a head tucked into eight puffy arms, drawn with flat cartoon shading. One file, [`design/poulpy-3d/model.mjs`](https://github.com/tkint/coach-poulpy/blob/main/design/poulpy-3d/model.mjs), describes his shape; the [Poulpy in 3D](?path=/docs/brand-poulpy-in-3d--docs) page of the component workshop draws it live, with a page for each of [his moves](?path=/docs/brand-poulpy-in-3d--docs), and [`design/build-poulpy-3d.mjs`](https://github.com/tkint/coach-poulpy/blob/main/design/build-poulpy-3d.mjs) writes it as glTF files. He is not in the apps yet: this is the reference to build from.

<Story of={Live.Model} />

## The rules of the shape

These were settled with the owner on the first model; the reasons are in [Brand decisions](?path=/docs/brand-decisions--docs#14-poulpy-in-3d-a-bubble-plush-in-flat-shading).

- **Chibi, never realistic.** A big round head, big eyes, short arms. The face is the 2D drawing's, pressed onto the head, so every [drawing](?path=/docs/brand-drawings--docs) and the model show the same Poulpy.
- **The head is tucked in.** It sinks into the arms, which wrap around its base, instead of resting on top of them.
- **Eight arms, always down.** They lie on the floor as on the plush; a mood shows on his face and in his colour, never by lifting an arm. When he [jumps](?path=/docs/brand-poulpy-moves-little-jumps--docs) they hang under him.
- **The other side is underneath.** Each arm is one smooth shape, the side's colour on top and the other side's colour below a low line, with no ridge or shelf between them. The base of the head is cut at the same height, so the whole underside is one colour: ember under the blue side, blue under the ember side.
- **Flat, like a drawing.** Plain token colours, one soft shadow band and one faint gleam. No gloss, no reflections, no fabric texture.
- **The light belongs to the room.** It comes from the viewer's upper left and stays there: the shade and the gleam slide over Poulpy as he turns, they are never painted on him.
- **The outline is optional and off by default.** It is there for small sizes or busy backgrounds.


## His six moods

The model makes the six [moods](?path=/docs/brand-moods--docs) of the drawings: the same faces, pressed onto the head feature by feature, and the same shades, from the `mood` tokens. The side of the plush follows the mood, so the three ember moods show blue underneath.

<Story of={Live.Moods} />

- **The faces are the drawings'.** Each face in `model.mjs` is written in the 2D drawing's own coordinates, so the two can be read side by side and a change to one is copied to the other.
- **A mood changes his face and his shade, never his shape.** Heavy lids, brows, a smirk or clenched teeth lie on the head like the eyes do; his arms stay down.


## His twelve poses

The model also takes the twelve [poses](?path=/docs/brand-moods--docs) of the drawings, each in the shade of its mood. They are in [`design/poulpy-3d/poses.mjs`](https://github.com/tkint/coach-poulpy/blob/main/design/poulpy-3d/poses.mjs), built on the shape and the faces of `model.mjs`.

<Story of={Live.Poses} />

- **What he wears is solid.** The sweatband goes all the way around his head, the nightcap sits on it, the medal rests on his front arm and the dumbbell lies on the floor beside him: turn him and they turn with him.
- **What is on him is on his skin.** The plasters and the vein are laid against his head where the drawing has them and wrapped around it; sweat and tears are part of his face. Turn him and they stay where they are.
- **The comic effects stay flat and face the viewer.** Sparks, confetti, puffs, bubbles and lettering are the drawing's own, standing in front of him or behind him, and they keep facing whoever looks while he turns.
- **Cocky has no halo and no "PR!" badge in 3D.** The owner dropped them; his sparks stay, and become solid stars when he [winks](?path=/docs/brand-poulpy-moves-the-cocky-wink--docs).
- **He still never lifts an arm.** Standing tall stretches his arms taller and lifts his head with them; Side glance leans his head. Nothing else moves.
- **The loader is his outline from underneath, drawn frame by frame, with loose tentacles.** It is made from the model itself, seen from straight below, with his tentacles wider and shorter than in the other pictures so that neighbours touch at their base. Only the edge of his shape is drawn, in the brand blue and see-through, as the old loader was, rounded, with no line inside. Each tentacle is loose: it bends on the same arm springs as his turn (`createFollow` in `motion.mjs`) and trails behind the turn. A cycle is 48 frames in one sheet, showing how the tentacles hang at that moment relative to his body; the apps and the website play them in turn and turn the whole thing smoothly. They are kept once, in `design/poulpy-3d/loader`, and every platform reads them from there. He swings half a turn one way and then half a turn the other (from -180° to 180°), forever, once every 3.6 s (once every 12 s with reduced motion), easing at each end. The other version only turns clockwise, a full turn every 3.6 s, with his tentacles trailing the same all the time, so it is one picture (`clockwise` on the phones, `spin="clockwise"` on the web). Which frame and how far it is turned is `LoaderSwing` in the shared Kotlin, and `PoulpyLoader` on Android and iOS, `MobilePoulpyLoader` and `CpPoulpyLoader` in the workshop all follow it.


## His pictures

Where the apps and the website do not need him live, they take a picture of him: one for each of the six moods and twelve poses, painted from the model, and the frames of the loader. They are in [`design/poulpy-3d/pictures`](https://github.com/tkint/coach-poulpy/blob/main/design/poulpy-3d/pictures), one PNG each at 744 by 678 pixels, the same frame as the drawings they replace so a picture can take a drawing's place without moving anything. **They are transparent around him**, with no background and no tile, so they sit on a light or a dark screen alike; the preview below shows them on the page's own background.

<Story of={Live.Pictures} />

- **They are painted by our own script.** [`design/poulpy-3d/picture.mjs`](https://github.com/tkint/coach-poulpy/blob/main/design/poulpy-3d/picture.mjs) draws what `model.mjs` and `poses.mjs` build, pixel by pixel, in plain JavaScript with the look of `LOOK`: the same flat shading, gleam and floor shadow as the live view. No browser or graphics card is involved, so every machine writes the same pixels, as for the app icons.
- **Every picture is taken from the same place.** He is seen from a little above and face on, close enough to fill the frame, and the same distance for all of them so he is the same size from one to the next.
- **The floor shadow is part of the picture**: a see-through dark blue that fades to nothing, so it shows on a light screen and disappears on a dark one.
- **Generated, never edited.** `node design/build-poulpy-pictures.mjs` writes them and CI runs it with `--check`. Change the model, a face or a pose, then regenerate.


## His moves

He moves in 3D too. Each move has its own page in the component workshop, so only one runs at a time:

- [Turning in short steps](?path=/docs/brand-poulpy-moves-turning--docs): his idle.
- [Little jumps](?path=/docs/brand-poulpy-moves-little-jumps--docs) on the spot.
- [Jumping around](?path=/docs/brand-poulpy-moves-jumping-around--docs): the same jumps, each turning him.
- [The champion jumps for joy](?path=/docs/brand-poulpy-moves-the-champion--docs), his medal bouncing and confetti flying.
- [The cocky one winks](?path=/docs/brand-poulpy-moves-the-cocky-wink--docs), and stars pop up around him.

All of them are one file, [`design/poulpy-3d/motion.mjs`](https://github.com/tkint/coach-poulpy/blob/main/design/poulpy-3d/motion.mjs), next to the shape. A preview only moves while it is on screen, and starts paused for anyone who asked their device for less motion; an app must do the same.


## Using the model

| File | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| [poulpy_blue.glb](https://github.com/tkint/coach-poulpy/blob/main/design/poulpy-3d/poulpy_blue.glb) | The blue, smiling side, as binary glTF |
| [poulpy_ember.glb](https://github.com/tkint/coach-poulpy/blob/main/design/poulpy-3d/poulpy_ember.glb) | The ember, grumpy side, as binary glTF |
| [poulpy_blue_turn.glb](https://github.com/tkint/coach-poulpy/blob/main/design/poulpy-3d/poulpy_blue_turn.glb) | The blue side with the animation `turn`: one full turn in short steps, made to loop |
| [poulpy_ember_turn.glb](https://github.com/tkint/coach-poulpy/blob/main/design/poulpy-3d/poulpy_ember_turn.glb) | The ember side with the same animation |
| [`design/poulpy-3d/model.mjs`](https://github.com/tkint/coach-poulpy/blob/main/design/poulpy-3d/model.mjs) | The shape itself, as plain JavaScript with no dependency |
| [`design/poulpy-3d/poses.mjs`](https://github.com/tkint/coach-poulpy/blob/main/design/poulpy-3d/poses.mjs) | His twelve poses, the same way |
| [`design/poulpy-3d/motion.mjs`](https://github.com/tkint/coach-poulpy/blob/main/design/poulpy-3d/motion.mjs) | How he moves, the same way |

The glTF files open in any 3D tool or engine. Poulpy stands on the floor (y = 0, y up) and faces +z; his head is about one unit from centre to edge. In the two files that stand still, each part is its own named mesh (`head`, `head_lining`, `arm_1` to `arm_8` and their `_lining`, `eye_left`, `eye_left_shine`, `cheek_left`, `mouth`, `gleam`, plus `brow_left` and `brow_right` on the ember side; left and right are Poulpy's own), so a part can be recoloured, hidden or animated on its own.

The two `_turn` files hold the same meshes, rigged. The node `turn` faces him and `squash` under it carries his head and face; each arm is skinned to `turn` and to its own chain of three joints, `arm_1_bend_1` to `arm_1_bend_3` from the head outwards. The animation `turn` plays one full turn at 30 frames a second and ends where it starts, so any player can loop it. It is a recording of the springs at their design values: an engine that wants them live, to change the softness or to react to something, runs `createTurn()` from `motion.mjs` on the same joints, as the workshop's preview does.

A glTF file only carries shapes and plain matte colours. The look is the renderer's job, and `LOOK` in `model.mjs` gives its numbers: the light's direction as the viewer sees it, the shadow band's strength, where the gleam sits, and the outline's width and tint. A renderer that wants the gleam to follow the light drops the `gleam` mesh from the file and asks `gleamPatch(direction)` for a new one whenever Poulpy or the camera turns. [`poulpy3dScene.ts`](https://github.com/tkint/coach-poulpy/blob/main/web/storybook/stories/brand/poulpy3dScene.ts), which draws the workshop's preview with three.js, is the worked example.


## Changing the design

Everything that defines him is at the top of `model.mjs`, in three plainly named objects:

- `SHAPE`: the size of the head and how deep it sits, the number, size and reach of the arms, the height of the line between the two colours, and where the face sits.
- `FACES`: the eyes, lids, brows, mouth and cheeks of each face, feature by feature, in the coordinates of the 2D drawings of `design/build-poulpy.mjs`.
- `MOODS`: for each of his six moods, the side of the plush and the face he makes. `buildPoulpy3d({ mood, tone })` builds him in one, tinted with that mood's `mood` token.
- `LOOK`: the light, the shadow band, the gleam and the outline.

His poses are in `poses.mjs`: `POSES` gives each one its mood, its face, what he wears, what lies on his head and the effects around him, all in the drawing's coordinates, and `buildPoulpyPose({ pose })` builds it.

How he moves is in `motion.mjs`: `TURN` for his turn, `JUMP` for his jump, `CHEER` for the champion's, `WINK` for the cocky one's and `RIG` for where the arms bend.

His colours are the `color.poulpy` tokens of [`design/tokens.json`](https://github.com/tkint/coach-poulpy/blob/main/design/tokens.json), never written into the model.

Edit, then regenerate and look at the workshop's page (`npm run storybook` in `web/`):

```sh
node design/build-poulpy-3d.mjs
```

CI runs it with `--check` and fails when the committed glTF files no longer match `model.mjs` and `motion.mjs`. A new mood in 3D starts as a new entry in `FACES` and `MOODS`, a new pose as a new entry in `POSES`; a new move starts next to `TURN`, `JUMP`, `CHEER` and `WINK` in `motion.mjs`, with a page of its own in the workshop. Both follow the [brand rules](?path=/docs/brand-character--docs) like any drawing.

<Meta title="Brand/Poulpy looks/Autumn" />

# Poulpy in autumn

**Draft.** A look for the season, to review here before it goes anywhere else: Poulpy, happy and cosy in a little white and red striped scarf, while maple leaves fall around him.

<Story of={Live.Autumn} />

- **He is happy Poulpy, on the blue side.** A look is never a mood of its own: it is his happy face and shade, with cheeks a little rosier from the cold.
- **The scarf is part of him.** It goes all the way around his head where his arms meet it, sinks a little into their soft tops and is knotted on his left, above his second arm. Its two ends lie over that arm and hang off its tip, with a short fringe. Turn him and it turns with him; it never covers his smile.
- **The scarf's red is poppy, not the error crimson nor the ember side.** Off-white wool (`#FBF6EE`) and poppy red (`#E5373A`), brighter and warmer than the crimson of errors (`#C8264A`) and redder than the ember (`#D9622B`). With its white stripes it reads as knitting, never as a state.
- **The leaves are flat, like the comic effects of his poses.** Three autumn oranges, each a five-lobed maple leaf. Falling, a leaf faces the viewer and swings from side to side like a pendulum: it falls quickest through the middle of a swing and tilts up at each end, and now and then half turns over. On the floor it settles flat, stays a moment and goes, and another one falls from the top. They fall around him, never through him.
- **He sways and breathes.** Once every 6.4 s he turns a little to one side and the other, his head leaning a moment later, and his head stretches and settles with his breath. His arms trail the sway on the same springs as his turn, and they stay on the floor.
- **Every run is the same.** Where each leaf falls and how it swings comes from a fixed list, not from chance, and the leaves have already been falling for a while when he appears.

`AUTUMN` in [`design/poulpy-3d/looks/autumn.mjs`](https://github.com/tkint/coach-poulpy/blob/main/design/poulpy-3d/looks/autumn.mjs) holds every number: his cheeks, the scarf, the leaves and his idle. `buildAutumn()` builds him in his scarf and `createAutumn()` runs the leaves and the sway live. Like the moves, it is a preview: it is not in the glTF files nor in the apps' pictures.

**Still open:** its values (the scarf's colours, how many leaves fall and how fast, how far he sways).

# Poulpy the cook

**Draft.** A look to review here before it goes anywhere else: Poulpy dressed up as a cook who is sure of everything, in a tall white toque worn a little askew, with a big curled French moustache and a confident grin.

<Story of={Live.Chef} />

- **His face** is a small, confident toothy grin, short from top to bottom, its top tucked under the moustache so only a few teeth show. His eyes are wide open and both brows are up, set high so the moustache has room. It is our own drawing, made for Poulpy.
- **The moustache is solid and big.** A thick, wide handlebar, a rounded volume that stands out from his face like the toque does, tapering from his middle to two tips that curl up beside his eyes, never over them. It is shaded like him, in a dark a little lighter than his ink, belongs to his face (it goes with his head and twitches) and lies over the grin's top teeth.
- **The toque is solid.** A plain band, then a puff with soft folds and a light crease in each. It sits on his head, leans 9° to his left and 5° back, and goes wherever his head goes.
- **His idle is small.** He stands still, then puffs himself up: his chin goes up 6° and his head grows a little taller, on a spring, and while he holds it his moustache twitches twice, tips up. Then he settles back. `CHEF` in `motion.mjs` holds the timing.
- **Still Poulpy.** Proud, on the blue side, eight tentacles on the floor and no arms (brand decision 8). Walk around him: the toque and the moustache stay where they belong.

The look is in [`design/poulpy-3d/looks/chef.mjs`](https://github.com/tkint/coach-poulpy/blob/main/design/poulpy-3d/looks/chef.mjs): `TOQUE`, `MOUSTACHE`, `SMILE` and `CHEF_FACE`. It is a preview only: not in the glTF files, the pictures or the apps.

<Meta title="Brand/Poulpy looks/The DJ" />

# Poulpy the DJ

**Draft.** A look to review here before it goes anywhere else: Poulpy behind a set of decks, his headset on, playing. His eyes are shut and he smiles a little: he is into the music and enjoying himself. His head bobs to the beat, he scratches one record while the other turns, and music notes float up around him.

<Story of={Live.Dj} />

- **He wears a headset.** A padded band over the top of his head and a round cup over each side, ember with a gold cap. It is solid and goes wherever his head goes.
- **The decks lie on the floor in front of him.** One low console with a turntable each side and the mixer in the middle, low enough that his face stays clear. Turn the view and they stay where they are.
- **He plays with the tips of his arms, never lifting one.** His front arm lies on the mixer and the two beside it on the records, as they lie on the floor. The scratch is his arm sliding over the record, the way his arms slide when he turns, and the record rocks with it; the other record keeps turning.
- **His head bobs, only just.** On each beat it nods forward a couple of degrees and dips a little, then comes back up, leaning to one side and then the other, on springs so it never snaps.
- **The notes float up like the cocky one's stars pop.** One starts every two beats, a little past its size and back, floats up, sways and rocks, then shrinks away. They are comic effects, so they are flat and keep facing whoever looks, like the poses' sparks, each with a white edge so it reads on a light or a dark page.
- **Blue side, happy.** He is in the happy shade, with the happy one's blush.
- **Still, he stands at the decks** with nothing moving and no notes, as for reduced motion; the still notes of `buildDj()` are there for a picture, if the look gets one.

`DJ_KIT`, `DJ_FACE` and `DJ_NOTES` in [`design/poulpy-3d/looks/dj.mjs`](https://github.com/tkint/coach-poulpy/blob/main/design/poulpy-3d/looks/dj.mjs) hold the headset, the decks, his face and the notes; `DJ` in `motion.mjs` holds the beat, the bob, the scratch and how the notes float, and `createDj()` runs it live. Like the other moves it is a preview, not in the glTF files.

**Still open:** its values (the tempo, how far his head bobs, how often a note floats up).

<Meta title="Brand/Poulpy looks/Jetpack" />

# Poulpy with a jetpack

**Draft.** A look to review here before it goes anywhere else: Poulpy in a costume and a move of his own, for fun moments. He wears a little rocket pack and zooms from one side to the other, smiling with his eyes shut, flames and smoke under him and his tentacles trailing.

<Story of={Live.Jetpack} />

- **The pack is solid, part of him.** Two little white rockets on a plate across the back of his head, each with a round blue nose, a blue stripe, a fin and a steel nozzle. They lean in at the top so their nozzles point down and a little out, clear of his tentacles. Turn him and they turn with him; face on, you see their sides and their flames.
- **He is enjoying the ride.** His face is [the DJ's](?path=/docs/brand-poulpy-looks-the-dj--docs): eyes shut in two happy arcs, a small smile, a little lopsided, and the happy blush, on the blue side in the happy shade. Flying is fun, never a chore. As he pushes off, his smile widens a touch, and nothing else on his face moves. His head widens a little with the push and wobbles back as he stops. `jetpackFace()` gives his face at any point between hovering and dashing. He does not blink for now; a natural, infrequent blink may come later.
- **The flames and the smoke are comic effects.** Each flame is three flat layers, orange, yellow and pale cream, facing the viewer like the sparks and puffs of the poses and pointing the way its nozzle does. They are fire, gold and yellow, never the ember of his grumpy side. They flicker and burn longer as he pushes off. The smoke is the fuming pose's puffs, light with a grey-blue edge: they leave the flames' tips, grow, drift and shrink away, and stay in the room, so he leaves a trail as he zooms. Overlapping puffs make one cloud with one outline.
- **He zooms, banks and looks where he goes.** He hovers well off the floor, bobbing, and glides from one side to the other, easing in and out, with a short hover at each end. Going sideways he banks into the turn and turns his face a little towards where he is going.
- **His tentacles hang and trail, he never lifts them.** In the air they hang heavier than in [a jump](?path=/docs/brand-poulpy-moves-little-jumps--docs), as if he pulled a few G's, and they lag behind him on the same three bends: they trail as he sets off and settle as he stops, with hardly a swing past him, because the G's weigh them down. Brand decision 8 holds: he never raises a tentacle himself. **Soft arms** loosens them.

The look is `JETPACK` and `buildPoulpyJetpack()` in [`design/poulpy-3d/looks/jetpack.mjs`](https://github.com/tkint/coach-poulpy/blob/main/design/poulpy-3d/looks/jetpack.mjs); the flight is `ZOOM` and `createZoom()` in [`motion.mjs`](https://github.com/tkint/coach-poulpy/blob/main/design/poulpy-3d/motion.mjs). It is a live preview, not in the glTF files or the pictures.

**Still open:** where he will show (probably at the end of a session, where the screen has room for him to zoom about; nothing is built there until this page is agreed), and its values (how far and how fast he zooms, how heavy his tentacles hang, how long the flames burn).

<Meta title="Brand/Poulpy looks/Rodolphe" />

# Rodolphe, the red-nosed reindeer

**Draft.** A festive look to review here before it goes anywhere else: Poulpy dresses up as a red-nosed reindeer, our own take on the old idea and no one else's character, and he is very happy about it.

<Story of={Live.Rodolphe} />

- **Always the blue side, always happy.** Rodolphe is a treat, so he never wears the ember side and never frowns.
- **A felt reindeer headband.** A flat, broad strip goes over the top of his head, leaning a little back. Seen from above it is wide front to back; seen from the front it is a solid felt band, and it stops well above his sides. Two big, chunky dark-brown felt antlers sit low on it, close to his head. Each is a fat beam that rises and bows out, with two round tines branching outwards and a little gold jingle bell on every tip. Below and outside each antler is a felt reindeer ear, tan outside and cream inside, pointing outwards. At the front of each antler's base is a full cluster of holly: six round-ended green leaves fanned out, none pointing down towards his eyes, and five red berries in the middle. It is all soft and plush, with no points, and the design is our own.
- **A round, shiny red nose.** A bulb half out of his face, between his eyes and his smile, with a white dot of light like his eyes have. His happy face moves up a little to make room for it and his smile is a little smaller.
- **A white and red striped scarf.** Puffy knitted pieces all around the base of his head, sitting on his arms: lower in front, under his smile, higher behind. It is knotted over his front right arm and its two ends lie along that arm. Turn the view and everything he wears goes round with him.
- **His reds are not an alarm.** The nose and the scarf are a bright, warm cherry (`#F2353A`, `#E2373F`), lighter and yellower than the error crimson (`#C8264A`) and redder than any ember shade, and they only ever show on blue. Nothing about him reads as an error or as anger. The berries are the scarf's red. The antlers are `#5E3A22`, the headband `#9A6A42`, the bells the medal's gold `#F0B53A`, the ears `#C89A6A` with a `#F5E6CC` inside and the holly `#2E8B4E`; the nose lights up towards `#FF8C8C` and its glow is `#FF5A4E`, fading out.
- **Flat, like the rest of him.** One shadow band, the plain colours below, no gloss: the nose's shine is a white dot, as on his eyes.
- **He sways to a tune.** A step to his left, a step to his right: his body turns a little each way on a spring and his arms trail behind it as they do when he turns, his head leans into each step and bobs on the beat, and the scarf's ends swing behind. Every eight beats he holds still for two, his nose still glowing.
- **His nose glows on the beat.** Every other beat it lights up, swells a hair and a warm glow blooms in front of it, then it fades back. The glow is light, so it belongs to whoever draws him, like the gleam; the model only holds the nose.
- **No arms.** His eight arms stay on the floor; the dance is in his body, his head and the scarf. The scarf's ends lie on an arm, they are not held.

[`design/poulpy-3d/looks/rodolphe.mjs`](https://github.com/tkint/coach-poulpy/blob/main/design/poulpy-3d/looks/rodolphe.mjs) holds the whole look, built like a pose and moving like a move: `FACE` and `COLOURS`, the shapes in `buildRodolphe()`, and `IDLE`, the dance's timing and springs, which `createRodolpheIdle()` runs. `PoulpyRodolphe.vue` beside this page adds the glow. It is a preview only: not in the glTF files, the pictures or the apps.

**Still open:** whether he keeps the name Rodolphe; when he would show (a December look, a reward, a choice in settings); whether the dance is his idle or a move he does when tapped; and whether he goes into the glTF files and the pictures once agreed.

<Meta title="Brand/Poulpy looks/Winter" />

# Winter Poulpy

**Draft.** A look for the cold months, to review here before it goes anywhere else: Poulpy, happy, in fluffy ear muffs and a scarf, while snow falls around him and his breath shows in the cold air.

<Story of={Live.Winter} />

- **What he wears is solid and part of him**, like the poses' props. The set is a warm cream and a deep berry: never ember, which is his angry side, and not the autumn scarf's red, and both stand out against his blue.
- **The scarf is the [autumn look](?path=/docs/brand-poulpy-looks-autumn--docs)'s**, exactly: the same shape, size and place, knot and ends, built with its own code, in cream with berry stripes.
- **The ear muffs sit where the DJ's headset does**: a thin berry band over his head and a big fluffy cream muff on each side, over where his ears would be, covered in small tufts so its outline is furry.
- **He is happy, on the blue side.** His face is the happy one, with rosier cheeks from the cold. Winter is cosy, never cold and miserable.
- **Snow falls around him.** A few six-armed crystals in frost blue, which shows on a light page and a dark one. Each falls at its own pace, sways and turns on itself, and melts where it lands. The flakes are flat and face the viewer, like the comic effects, but they are in the room: walk around him and they stay where they are. They never fall through him. Every run is the same: where each flake falls comes from a fixed list, as the champion's confetti does.
- **His breath shows.** Each time he breathes out, his head squashes a little and three small puffs of mist leave his mouth and drift off to the side he looks to, clear of his eyes, rising, growing and fading. They are pale and soft-edged, nothing like the fuming pose's puffs: cold breath, not anger.
- **His idle is gentle.** He looks a little to one side, then to the other, on a soft spring; his head leans with him and his arms trail behind, as in his turn. He never lifts an arm.

`WINTER` in [`design/poulpy-3d/looks/winter.mjs`](https://github.com/tkint/coach-poulpy/blob/main/design/poulpy-3d/looks/winter.mjs) holds every number: the colours, the ear muffs, the sway, the breath and the snow. `buildWinterPoulpy()` builds him and `createWinter()` runs his idle. import { Meta, Story } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as Live from '../Brand.stories'

<Meta title="Brand/Poulpy moves/Turning" />

# Turning in short steps

His idle move: Poulpy likes to turn around on the spot, a short step of 20 to 30 degrees at a time, stopping after each one. Fifteen steps bring him all the way around, in about 17 seconds, and then he goes again.

<Story of={Live.Turning} />

His arms are not stiff. Each one bends at three places, and every bend is a small spring: when he steps the arms trail behind, when he stops they swing a little past him and settle, the tips last. The controls of the turning model are there to try other feels, and each shows its value so a setting can be quoted and written into the design. **Step** sets how far he turns each time, from 1 to 180 degrees, keeping the small differences between one step and the next; 24 is the design. **Soft arms** loosens or stiffens those springs: 1 is the design, 0 is the stiff plush with no springs at all and 4 is very floppy. **Speed** plays the whole move faster or slower, 1 being the design. The two arrows pick the direction, seen from above; the design turns anticlockwise, to his left.

- **The arms slide, they never lift.** Every bend turns flat on the floor, so the move keeps the plush's shape as the [brand rules](?path=/docs/brand-character--docs) ask.
- **He winds up, then goes.** A small lean back before each step, a quick turn, and a slight rock past the mark as he stops.
- **The head dips as he turns** and bounces back, by a few hundredths of its height, widening to keep its volume. His face rides along with it.
- **No two steps or arms are quite alike.** The steps vary between 20 and 30 degrees and the pauses between 0.45 and 0.75 seconds, and each arm's springs are a little stiffer or softer than its neighbours', so the arms fall out of step with each other.
- **Reduced motion keeps him still.** The preview starts paused for anyone who asked their device for less motion, and an app must do the same.

`TURN` at the top of `motion.mjs` holds every number: the steps and pauses, the wind-up, how eager and how bouncy his body is, how soft each length of arm is, how much the floor holds the arms back and how far the head dips. `createTurn()` runs it live, as the workshop's page does, and `bakeTurn()` writes it down frame by frame for the glTF files.

import { Meta, Story } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as Live from '../Brand.stories'

<Meta title="Brand/Poulpy moves/Little jumps" />

# Little jumps

Poulpy can also jump on the spot. He tucks his head down into his arms, which widen flat on the floor, then he goes up. His arms are part of him: their base goes up with his head and their tips hang a little lower, the last to leave the floor. In the air he tilts to one side, the other side at the next jump, and as he lands his head goes a little down into his arms before he stands again.

<Story of={Live.Jumping} />

**The jump is a preview, still being tuned.** It runs live here and is not in the glTF files yet: its values are written into them once the owner has settled them on this page. Every control shows its value so a setting can be quoted. Heights are in the model's units, where his head is about 1 from centre to edge.

| Control | What it sets | Design |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Height** | How far he goes up | 0.34 |
| **Tuck** | How far his head goes down into his arms before the jump | 0.16 |
| **Landing** | How far his head goes down into his arms as he lands | 0.10 |
| **Spread** | How far his arms slide outwards when his head is tucked all the way in | 0.14 |
| **Hang** | How heavy his arms are, so how low their tips hang in the air | 1 |
| **Lean** | How far he tilts to the side in the air, in degrees | 7 |
| **Pause** | Seconds he stands between two jumps, on average | 0.55 |
| **Soft arms** | How loosely his arms hang and trail, as for the turn | 1 |
| **Speed** | Plays the whole move faster or slower | 1 |

- **His head never leaves his arms.** It goes down into them, to tuck and to land, and never up out of them: when he goes up they go with him.
- **His arms widen as his head comes down.** They stay flat on the floor and slide outwards, as a plush does when it is pressed.
- **The arms hang, he never raises them.** Up and down, each arm bends at the same three places as when he turns. A spring holds each length level with the one before it, its weight pulls it down and the floor stops it: the tips leave the floor last, hang under him in the air and touch down first. A length may hang nearly straight down when it has to. On the side he tilts to, the arms lie flat against the floor.
- **His head squashes and stretches.** It widens as it tucks in and as he lands, and thins a little while it moves fast, keeping its volume.
- **Reduced motion keeps him still**, as for the turn.

`JUMP` in `motion.mjs` holds the jump's numbers, next to `TURN`, and `createJump()` runs it live.

<Meta title="Brand/Poulpy moves/The champion" />

# The champion jumps for joy

The Champion pose, moving: he cannot hold still. His jumps are the [little jumps](?path=/docs/brand-poulpy-moves-little-jumps--docs), higher, leaning more and closer together, and two things answer them.

<Story of={Live.Cheering} />

- **His medal has its own weight.** It hangs on its ribbon from under his head and rests on his front arm. When he drops it floats up off him, then falls back on his arm with a small bounce; when he tilts it slides to that side and wobbles back. Nothing is drawn by hand: it is a weight on a hinge, pulled down and stopped by his arm.
- **Confetti flies at each jump.** A burst leaves the floor around him as he does, goes up past his head and flutters down, tumbling. It lands flat and stays on the floor until it flies again, so the floor fills up as he goes on. The pieces are solid here and belong to the room: turn the view and they stay where they are. The still pose keeps its flat confetti.
- **Every run is the same.** Where each piece starts and how it tumbles comes from a fixed list, not from chance, so the move can be written into a file later.
- **He still never lifts an arm.** His joy is in the jump, his face, the medal and the confetti.

The controls are the jump's, starting from the champion's own values: Height 0.50, Lean 9 and Pause 0.26. `CHEER` in `motion.mjs` holds those, the medal's weight, bounce and reach and the confetti's numbers, and `createCheer()` runs it live. Like the jump it is a preview, not in the glTF files yet.

<Meta title="Brand/Poulpy moves/The cocky wink" />

# The cocky one winks

The Cocky pose, moving. He looks at you with both eyes wide open, then shuts one eye (his right, unless told otherwise), lifts the other brow and his mouth slides into the cocky smirk. He holds it, opens his eye and starts again.

<Story of={Live.Winking} />

- **His face moves, feature by feature.** The eye narrows to a line and the line bends into the wink; the brow and the mouth go from plain to cocky with it. `winkFace()` in `poses.mjs` gives his face at any point between the two, in the drawing's coordinates like every face.
- **His head goes with it.** It leans a little to the side of the eye he shuts and dips, on a spring, then comes back.
- **The stars come with the wink.** There are none while his eyes are open. As the eye shuts they pop up one after the other, each a little past its size and back, and they leave when he opens it.
- **The stars are solid and they twinkle.** Each is a four-point star cut like a gem, in the room around him where the drawing has its sparks. It grows and shrinks, turns on itself and rocks, and no two keep the same time. Turn the view and they stay where they are.
- **No halo, no badge.** The drawing's glow and its "PR!" are not part of him in 3D.

The switch picks the eye he shuts, named for him: his right eye, the design, is on your left. His brow, his smirk and the lean of his head go to the other side with it.

`WINK` in `motion.mjs` holds the timing, the lean of his head and the stars' numbers, and `createWink()` runs it live. It is a preview, not in the glTF files yet.

# Getting angry, and calming down

Drafts for Home, to validate before anything is baked for the phones. Tapping Poulpy again and again makes him lose patience, and leaving him alone calms him down. Each change of mood is a full turn, and the face changes half way round; going down, the turn is **clockwise**.

First the whole run, with the variants chosen below:

<Story of={Live.Sequence} />

## One preview per transition

Each has three variants to compare. The turns are exactly 360 degrees.

### Normal to annoyed

After several taps he turns on the spot and comes out annoyed.

<Story of={Live.ToAnnoyed} />

### Annoyed to fuming

Tapped again, he turns once more and comes out fuming, with his fumes puffing behind him.

<Story of={Live.ToFuming} />

### Fuming back to annoyed

After a while he turns back, clockwise, and the fumes go.

<Story of={Live.CalmDown} />

### Annoyed back to normal

Later still, the same turn back to his normal self.

<Story of={Live.BackToNormal} />

How he answers a tap in each mood, with no transition, is on [Annoyed](?path=/docs/brand-poulpy-moves-annoyed--docs) and [Fuming](?path=/docs/brand-poulpy-moves-fuming--docs).

- **On the spot, with a hop, wind-up and whip** are three ways to make the same turn: feet on the floor, a small jump, or a lean back first that makes him rock past the mark. They are the move of [Turning](?path=/docs/brand-poulpy-moves-turning--docs) and [Jumping around](?path=/docs/brand-poulpy-moves-jumping-around--docs) with their values fixed.
